cases.prompt: Check whether our MAC tag comparison is constant time, and tell me how to test it.

any.why: can pinpoint the leak with Timecop

expectations: Identifies the early return on the first mismatching byte as a secret-dependent branch that leaks timing.
Fixes it by accumulating differences (for example OR of XORs) over every byte and deciding once at the end.
Describes a dudect test with two input classes (fixed versus random) run for minutes, not seconds, at the production optimization level.

cases.prompt: Our dudect run of 20 seconds on a build with -O0 showed no leak, so the code is constant time, right?

any.why: asks for a run of several minutes or more

none.why: does not agree that the code is proven constant time

expectations: Says no: a 20-second run is too short to detect weak signals; run for 5 to 10 minutes or more.
Explains that -O0 can hide leaks the optimizer introduces, so test at the production optimization level and on the target architecture.
Notes that a statistical test not finding a leak does not prove its absence, and points to formal tools for high assurance.
